text: Toronto adopted the city-wide Multi-Tenant Houses framework in December 2022, effective March 31, 2024, to establish consistent safety and licensing standards, preserve deeply affordable housing, and provide a pathway for previously unlicensed multi-tenant houses to enter legal, regulated operation. Since implementation, Municipal Licensing and Standards, in collaboration with the Housing Secretariat, Toronto Fire Services, Toronto Building and other City divisions, has undertaken significant work to implement the framework, process licence applications, support operators through the licensing process, and coordinate compliance and enforcement activities. As implementation continues, City Council would benefit from additional information on how key components of the framework are operating in practice. City Council request the Executive Director, Municipal Licensing and Standards and the Executive Director, Housing Secretariat, in consultation with the Chief Building Official and Executive Director, Toronto Building, and the Fire Chief and General Manager, Toronto Fire Services and other divisions and agencies as appropriate, to undertake a review and report back in the third quarter of 2027 to provide an update on the implementation of the multi-tenant houses framework, identify any barriers to licensing and compliance under the framework, and potential program changes to address these barriers, with the review to include an assessment of the Multi-Tenant Houses Renovation & Repair Program and the Operator Concierge Service together with any recommended changes. 2.
